lines.text: October inflation ran hot, and the yearly number is missing.
lines.say: October inflation ran hot, and the yearly number is missing.

lines.text: Prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% economists expected.
lines.say: Prices rose four tenths of a percent in October, above the three tenths economists expected.

lines.text: Core prices, without food and energy, rose 0.3%, versus 0.2% expected.
lines.say: Core prices, without food and energy, rose three tenths, versus two tenths expected.

lines.text: Why no yearly rate? The 2025 shutdown meant the government skipped collecting prices last October.
lines.say: Why no yearly rate? The twenty twenty-five shutdown meant the government skipped collecting prices last October.

lines.text: The last yearly reading was 3.7%, back in September.
lines.say: The last yearly reading was about three point seven percent, back in September.

lines.text: Groceries rose 0.4% too. Our math: a $100 cart now costs $100.40.
lines.say: Groceries rose four tenths of a percent too. Our math: a hundred dollar cart now costs a hundred dollars and forty cents.

lines.text: It's also the last CPI report before the Fed meets December 8 and 9.
lines.say: It's also the last consumer price report before the Fed meets on December eighth and ninth.

lines.text: Fed decisions flow into your card rate, loan rates and savings yield.
lines.say: And Fed decisions flow into your card rate, loan rates and savings yield.

lines.text: Simple test: if your raise is smaller than price growth, your real pay shrank.
lines.say: Simple test: if your raise is smaller than price growth, your real pay shrank.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: October inflation ran hot, and the yearly rate is missing
post.ig:
October inflation ran hot, and the yearly number is missing.
Prices rose 0.4% in October (economists expected 0.3%); core prices rose 0.3% vs 0.2% expected.
No 12-month rate this time: the 2025 shutdown meant no prices were collected in October 2025.
Groceries +0.4%: our math, a $100 cart is now $100.40. Last yearly rate: 3.7% in September.
It's the last CPI before the Fed meets Dec 8-9.
Sources: BLS (Nov 10, 2026), CNBC.
